items: Verify Before Hiring: Pull the contractor's license number and cross-reference it with your state's Contractor State License Board website to confirm it is active and matches the business name on the contract.

Verify Before Hiring: Check the license status, work classifications, and current bonding information on the CSLB website to confirm the contractor is authorized to perform your specific type of work.
Verify Before Hiring: Request a current Certificate of Insurance showing at least $1M general liability coverage and have the insurer confirm the policy directly within 24 hours.
Verify Before Hiring: Check your Secretary of State or county clerk records to confirm the business is registered, how long it has been operating, and who the registered agent is.
Protect Your Money: Never pay more than one-third of the total contract amount upfront at signing, or follow California's $1,000 or 10% maximum rule for residential projects.
Protect Your Money: Withhold the final payment until project completion, verified progress, and your final inspection and sign-off are complete.
Protect Your Money: Refuse to pay in cash and instead use check, credit card, or a payment platform with fraud protection so every transaction leaves a traceable record.
Protect Your Money: Tie all payment installments to concrete project milestones rather than calendar dates so money flows only as work is actually completed.

Lock Down the Contract: Verify the contract includes all required clauses: detailed scope of work, concrete start and completion dates, milestone-based payment schedule, change order process, warranty terms, termination rights, and lien waivers.
Lock Down the Contract: Never sign assignment of benefits agreements, blank change orders, or documents that release the contractor from liability without first consulting a lawyer.
Lock Down the Contract: Require every change order to be signed before extra work begins so all modifications are documented with your explicit approval.
Lock Down the Contract: Keep copies of all contracts, receipts, and written communications organized by project so you have documentation ready if you need to dispute charges or file a claim.
